<blog>

# Jeric Mark Caño — Portfolio Website

## 1. Project Introduction

### Purpose Statement
This is a personal portfolio website for **Jeric Mark C. Caño**, an IT professional, multimedia storyteller, and web developer from Iloilo, Philippines. The site showcases his work across video editing, photography, graphic design, and web development while highlighting his background in IT support, networking (CCNA), and community service.

### Core Goals and Objectives
- Present a professional online presence for job opportunities in IT support, multimedia production, and web development
- Showcase creative work including video edits, photography, and programming projects
- Demonstrate technical skills through the portfolio itself — built with modern HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
- Provide easy access to contact information and résumé download

### Target Audience
- Potential employers in IT, multimedia production, and web development
- Community organizations and church groups seeking multimedia services
- Professional network connections on LinkedIn and GitHub

---

## 2. Technical Architecture

This is a **static multi-page portfolio website** deployed on GitHub Pages. The architecture follows a simple but well-organized structure:

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Portfolio Site] --> B[Home Page - index.html]
    A --> C[About Page - about.html]
    A --> D[Projects Page - projects.html]
    
    B --> E[Shared Styles - style.css]
    C --> E
    D --> E
    
    B --> F[Shared Script - script.js]
    C --> F
    D --> F
    
    E --> G[Design System Variables]
    E --> H[Component Styles]
    E --> I[Animations & Effects]
    
    F --> J[Scroll Progress]
    F --> K[Mobile Navigation]
    F --> L[Reveal Animations]
    F --> M[Video Player Lazy Load]
    F --> N[Image Lightbox]
    
    O[External Dependencies] --> P[Typed.js Library]
    O --> Q[Google Fonts]
    O --> R[Google Drive Videos]
```

### Design Patterns
- **Semantic HTML5** structure with proper accessibility attributes
- **CSS Custom Properties** for consistent theming and design tokens
- **Progressive Enhancement** with graceful fallbacks for reduced motion
- **Lazy Loading** for performance optimization
- **SVG Sprite System** for icon management
- **Mobile-First Responsive Design** with fluid typography and layouts

### System Relationships
The three main pages share common components through the shared stylesheet and JavaScript file, creating a cohesive user experience while maintaining clean separation of concerns.

---

## 3. Key Implementation

### Main Entry Points
- **`index.html`** - Landing page with hero section, skill showcase, and call-to-action buttons
- **`about.html`** - Detailed biography, journey timeline, and photo gallery with lightbox functionality
- **`projects.html`** - Video project showcase with lazy-loaded Google Drive players and photography grid

### Core Modules

#### Styling System (`style.css`)
- **Design Tokens**: CSS custom properties define colors, spacing, typography, and animation curves
- **Component Library**: Reusable components like buttons, cards, chips, and navigation elements
- **Animation System**: Scroll-triggered reveals, floating elements, and smooth transitions
- **Responsive Grid Layouts**: CSS Grid and Flexbox for flexible layouts across devices

#### Interactive Features (`script.js`)
- **Scroll Progress Indicator**: Visual progress bar at the top of the page
- **Mobile Navigation**: Accessible hamburger menu with keyboard navigation support
- **Intersection Observer**: Performance-optimized scroll animations with reduced motion support
- **Pointer Tracking**: Mouse spotlight effects on interactive elements
- **Typed.js Integration**: Animated role descriptions on the homepage
- **Lazy Video Loading**: Google Drive videos load only when users click play
- **Accessible Lightbox**: Full-screen image viewer with keyboard and touch navigation

### Configuration Approach
- **No build tools or frameworks** - Pure vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
- **External dependencies** managed through CDN links (Typed.js, Google Fonts)
- **SEO optimized** with meta tags, Open Graph protocol, and Schema.org markup
- **Accessibility first** with ARIA labels, semantic HTML, and keyboard navigation

### External Dependencies
- **Typed.js** (`vendor/typed.umd.js`) - Typing animation library for role descriptions
- **Google Fonts** - Inter and Space Grotesk typefaces loaded via CDN
- **Google Drive** - Video hosting and thumbnail generation for project showcases

### Integration Points
- **LinkedIn, GitHub, Facebook** - Social media profile links
- **Google Drive** - Video content hosting and thumbnail generation
- **GitHub Pages** - Static site hosting platform
- **Resume PDF** - Downloadable CV document

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[User Browser] --> B[HTML Structure]
    B --> C[CSS Styling Engine]
    B --> D[JavaScript Runtime]
    
    C --> E[Design System]
    C --> F[Layout Engine]
    C --> G[Animation System]
    
    D --> H[DOM Manipulation]
    D --> I[Event Handling]
    D --> J[API Calls]
    
    H --> K[Scroll Events]
    H --> L[Navigation Logic]
    H --> M[Media Players]
    
    I --> N[Touch Gestures]
    I --> O[Keyboard Navigation]
    I --> P[Mouse Interactions]
    
    J --> Q[Google Drive API]
    J --> R[Font Loading]
```

---

## 4. Key Features

### Functionality Overview

#### Hero Section with Typed Animation
The landing page features an animated introduction that cycles through different professional roles using the Typed.js library, creating an engaging first impression.

#### Skill Marquee
A continuously scrolling marquee displays key skills and competencies, providing quick visual scanning of capabilities.

#### Service Cards
Interactive cards showcasing core services (video editing, photography, graphic design, web development) with hover effects and gradient accents.

#### Video Project Showcase
Lazy-loaded video players that only initialize when users click the play button, optimizing initial page load performance.

#### Photography Gallery
Full-featured image gallery with lightbox functionality, supporting keyboard navigation, touch gestures, and accessible screen reader support.

#### Responsive Navigation
Mobile-first navigation system with hamburger menu, smooth animations, and full keyboard accessibility.

### Implementation Highlights

#### Advanced CSS Techniques
- **CSS Grid and Flexbox** for complex responsive layouts
- **Custom Properties** for consistent theming across the entire site
- **Advanced Selectors** and pseudo-elements for decorative effects
- **Hardware-accelerated animations** for smooth performance
- **Gradient text effects** and glass-morphism styling

#### Performance Optimizations
- **Lazy loading** for images and heavy media content
- **Intersection Observer API** for efficient scroll animations
- **Passive event listeners** for improved scroll performance
- **RequestAnimationFrame** for smooth pointer tracking
- **Reduced motion support** for accessibility compliance

#### Accessibility Features
- **Semantic HTML structure** with proper heading hierarchy
- **ARIA labels and roles** throughout the interface
- **Keyboard navigation** support for all interactive elements
- **Screen reader compatibility** with descriptive alt text
- **Focus management** in modal dialogs and navigation
- **Skip navigation link** for keyboard users

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Idle
    Idle --> Scrolling: User scrolls
    Scrolling --> HeaderShrink: Scroll > 10px
    HeaderShrink --> Scrolling: Continue scrolling
    Scrolling --> NavOpen: Mobile menu clicked
    NavOpen --> NavClosed: Menu closed
    NavClosed --> Scrolling: Resume scrolling
    
    Idle --> VideoLoading: Play button clicked
    VideoLoading --> VideoPlaying: iframe loaded
    VideoPlaying --> VideoPaused: Pause/stop
    VideoPaused --> VideoPlaying: Resume
    
    Idle --> LightboxOpen: Image clicked
    LightboxOpen --> LightboxNavigating: Arrow keys/swipe
    LightboxNavigating --> LightboxOpen: Navigate back
    LightboxOpen --> LightboxClosed: Close button/ESC
    LightboxClosed --> Idle
```

---

- [style.css](style.css)
- [script.js](script.js)

</blog>
